How can a website check your password without knowing it?
The trick is called hashing. A hash function chews up any text and spits out a fixed fingerprint.
Type “cat”, and SHA-256 gives you sixty-four characters of scrambled code.
Type “cats”, one letter more, and the whole fingerprint changes. Nothing is similar.
Same input always gives the same fingerprint. But you can't run it backwards.
So a site stores only the fingerprint. When you log in, it hashes what you typed and compares.
If hackers steal the list, they get fingerprints, not your password.
That's why a site that emails you your old password is doing it wrong.
The same idea checks downloads, powers Git, and sits inside Bitcoin.
